# Notes

- [Repo to follow along with code examples](https://github.com/TylerHillery/beejs-guide-ipc)

## Chapter 2. A `fork()` Primer

- A parent process `fork()`'s a child process (the new one) and the child process gets a *copy* of the parents' data.
- When a process dies it doesn't really go away, but instead a small remnant is waiting around for the parent process to pick up. The remnant contains the return value from the child process. So after a parent process `fork()`s a child process, it must `wait()` or `waitpid()` for that child process to exit. This is what allows all remnants of a child to vanish.
- The parent can ignore the `SIGCHLD` signal and then it won't have to `wait()`      
- If a chile process dies and has not been `wait()`ed on, it will show up in `ps` listing as `<defunct>`
- Oh interesting, so if a the parent dies before it `wait()`s for the child, the child is reparented to the `init` process (`PID 1`).
- Always ensure your parent process either ignores `SIGCHLD` or `wait()`s for all child it `fork()`s.
- `wait()` waits for whatever child process exists first, use `waitpid()` if you want to wait for a specific child

## Chapter 3. Signals

- A signal is just a way to interrupt another process.
- `SIGSTOP` is one signal you can send to stop that process and you can continue with `SIGCONT`.
- Many signals are predefined and the process has a default signal handler to deal with it.
- `SIGINT` is the interrupt signal that a process receives when the user hits `CTRL-C`. The default handler causes the process to exit.
- `SIGKILL` is a signal you **can't** add your own handler for. Same with the `SIGTSTOP`.
- `SIGTERM` is the default signal that gets sent from the `kill` command
- `SIGUSR1` and `SIGUSR2` are not reserved and are free to use for whatever.
- `kill()` is also the name of the sys call used to sends signals
- `raise()` is another way to raise a signal within the same process
- `sigaction()` is used to catch signals
- `write()` is async signal safe while `printf()` is not.

## Chapter 4. Signals Part II

- Signals only support an *raised at least once semantics*
- You can block signals with `sigprocmask()` where nothing will happen until you unblock it
- Reminder that several methods might fail with `EINTR` which means "interrupted", think Error: INTeRrupted, if a signal occurs when the function is running. Unless you set `SA_RESTART` the function will fail.
